objective: scripts/validate_continuity.py's step-8 reconciliation reported DIVERGED - the loudest of its four words - whenever the recorded baseline was in the object database but was not an ancestor of the observed main line. One ordering produces that shape innocently and it is the commonest state of a long-lived checkout: a main ref that has simply not been fetched sits BEHIND the baseline. The reconciliation now asks the reverse question at that branch and reports UNKNOWN, naming the staleness, where the tip is an ancestor of the baseline; DIVERGED is reached only where neither line contains the other. Filed from WP-112's own final review as #353, and closed here without a fifth word.
completed: THE DEFECT REPRODUCED BEFORE THE FIX AND MEASURED GONE AFTER IT, on the same clone rather than on two descriptions of one. `git clone` of the checkout, `git update-ref refs/remotes/origin/main <recorded baseline>~1`, then `python scripts/validate_continuity.py`: before, STATE_RECONCILIATION=DIVERGED with the reason 'the recorded baseline ... is present in this clone but is not an ancestor of refs/remotes/origin/main'; after, STATE_RECONCILIATION=UNKNOWN with 'refs/remotes/origin/main ... is an ancestor of the recorded baseline ..., so this clone's main ref is BEHIND the record rather than parted from it - it has not been fetched'. Both runs exit 0. That sequence is script controls 1 and 2 of scripts/wp114_controls.py, so it is a control rather than a paragraph.

ONE CALL AT THE DIVERGED BRANCH: `git merge-base --is-ancestor <tip> <baseline>`. Where the tip IS an ancestor of the baseline the main line is behind the record and the verdict is UNKNOWN with a reason naming the staleness - the degrade-rather-than-fail rule the shallow-clone branch already followed. Where it is not, DIVERGED stands, and its reason and its docstring entry now BOTH state the second direction, because WP-112 lost a round to the same claim surviving seventy lines above its repair.

THE VOCABULARY STAYS AT FOUR. #353 fixes it there explicitly and so does this package: UNKNOWN already means 'the history needed to judge is unavailable', which describes an unfetched clone accurately - what landed after the baseline genuinely cannot be read from a ref that predates it. A reader who needs the behind case told apart from the other four unavailabilities reads the REASON, and that wording is asserted rather than assumed.

THE THIRD OUTCOME IS DECIDED AND THE DECISION IS ARGUED IN A COMMENT THAT NAMES THE CASE. `merge-base --is-ancestor` answers 0, 1 or an error, and the error branch returns UNKNOWN rather than falling through to DIVERGED: when it is reached exactly one fact is established - the baseline is not an ancestor of the main line - and that fact alone is true of BOTH cases, so DIVERGED would assert the fault reading on evidence that does not exist, which is the defect #353 is about. The branch is reachable only by a timeout or an unrunnable git, because the identical call in the opposite direction succeeded a few lines above.

THE VERDICT IS STILL ADVISORY. Nothing added here appends to `errors`, changes the exit code or changes what the script validates. CI checks out with actions/checkout@v7 and no fetch-depth, so every CI run is shallow and takes the UNKNOWN branch before reaching any of this; #311 is what that rule protects.

THE WORST-CASE GIT BUDGET IS UNCHANGED AT 70 SECONDS, and the comment that states it now says why rather than repeating a count. There are SEVEN call sites where there were six, but `log` and the new reverse `merge-base` sit on opposite branches of the same `if`, so no run can make both; the worst case is still seven invocations, from the main-ref lookup spending two.

tests/test_resume_reconciliation.py gains five tests and three fixtures, every one CONSTRUCTED in a real repository rather than mocked: a main ref behind the baseline on refs/heads/main, the same on refs/remotes/origin/main, and a rebase beside the existing orphan-branch divergence. A fourth test measures the behind fixtures themselves - baseline present, baseline not an ancestor of the ref, ref an ancestor of the baseline - because a fixture that reproduces the wrong condition reports PASS.

THE TWO EXISTING DIVERGED FIXTURES ARE NOW CHECKED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Asserting only that the baseline is not an ancestor of the main line was the same one-way test the code was making, so a fixture that was merely BEHIND would have satisfied a test named for divergence. A control rebuilds the rebase fixture as a behind ref and shows that assertion refuse it.

THE LIVE-TREE TEST GREW A BEHIND BRANCH, and it is not hypothetical. A clone takes its origin/main from the source's refs/heads/main; the shared checkout's local main is at 67deeb2 while its origin/main is at d05afba - fetched and not pulled, the ordinary state - so with the baseline rolled to d05afba every control clone holds a record AHEAD of its own origin/main. That is #353's exact shape, and before this commit every one of those clones would have read DIVERGED.

observations: THE DEFECT WAS ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN IN THE FILE THAT CARRIED IT. `reconcile_recorded_state`'s docstring said in so many words that DIVERGED overstated its case, named the ordering that explains it, and cited the open issue - and the code went on printing it. A known defect documented beside itself is not a mitigated defect: every reader who trusts the word rather than the paragraph gets the wrong answer, and the resume protocol asks an agent to read the WORD.

THE HARNESS WAS THE DEFECT'S BEST WITNESS, and only after the record rolled. Before the roll every control clone read CONSISTENT on its live tree and nothing about #353 was live in the harness at all. After it, every clone holds a record ahead of its own origin/main - because a clone's origin/main is the source's refs/heads/main and the shared checkout is fetched but not pulled - so the live test takes the BEHIND branch and two controls that were isolated stop being isolated. The controls were run BOTH SIDES of the roll for exactly that reason; the numbers in this file are the second run.

A ONE-WAY TEST IN THE CODE HAD PRODUCED A ONE-WAY TEST IN THE FIXTURES. `test_the_diverged_reason_is_true_of_the_condition_that_reaches_it` asserted only that the baseline was not an ancestor of the main line - which is what the code asked - so a fixture that was merely behind would have satisfied a test named for divergence, and nothing would have said so. The second direction is asserted now and a control shows it refuse such a fixture. Where a test re-derives the code's own condition, it inherits the code's blind spots along with its logic.

THE BRIEF'S PREDICTION ABOUT THE LIVE READING WAS WRONG IN BOTH HALVES, AND MEASURING IT COST NOTHING. It said STATE_RECONCILIATION would move from CONSISTENT to LAG_EXPECTED. It stood at LAG_EXPECTED before the roll - WP-113 was recorded active and had landed on origin/main - and moved to CONSISTENT after it. Neither the direction nor the destination matched. Nothing was built on the prediction because the reading was taken rather than assumed, which is the whole of the rule this repository keeps re-learning.

THE THIRD OUTCOME OF A THREE-WAY CALL IS A DECISION, NOT AN OVERSIGHT, AND IT DESERVES THE COMMENT RATHER THAN THE CODE. Both answers are defensible: fall through to DIVERGED and you keep the loud word for a broken git; return UNKNOWN and a real divergence is under-reported while git is unwell. What settles it is that at that point the evidence for DIVERGED has not been gathered, and asserting a verdict on evidence you failed to collect is the shape of the defect being repaired.

A COUNT IS ONLY AS GOOD AS ITS FILTER, and #357 says so twice over. Grepping tests/ for the WORD `subprocess` returns six modules; grepping for the CALL returns four. The measurement control here re-derives both from the docstring's own printed command and refuses to pass if the two ever agree, because if they did the docstring's warning would be describing nothing.

THE CONTROL RUNNER IS THE THIRD COPY OF THE SAME HARNESS - wp112, wp113 and now wp114 each carry their own `edit`, `clone`, `run_suite` and `check_source_main_line`. That is the house shape and it was followed deliberately, but it is duplication of the kind WP-110 consolidated for `_norm`, and the next runner should probably import rather than copy.
assumptions: That `git merge-base --is-ancestor A B` exits 0 when A is an ancestor of B, 1 when it is not, and something else on error. That is the documented contract and the existing code already rests on it for the forward question; the new call rests on it for the reverse. Nothing here verifies git's own behaviour - a git that answered the reverse question wrongly would produce a confident wrong verdict, and no test in this repository would notice.

That a main ref which is an ancestor of the recorded baseline is a ref that has not been fetched. It is the overwhelmingly common cause and it is the one the reason names. It is not the only one: a deliberate reset of the published main line to an earlier commit produces the same shape and would be reported as staleness. Distinguishing the two needs the reflog or the remote, and neither is available to a read-only local call.

That the record's baseline is a commit on the line the main ref is meant to track. Everything above compares those two and nothing checks that the baseline was ever published; a baseline recorded from a branch that never merged would read as a main ref behind the record, which is the same words for a different situation.

That the validator's stdout format is unchanged, so scripts/build_control_page.py still parses it. The verdict line and the reason line keep their names and their position beside RESUME_DECISION; only the words in the reason changed. Measured by running the projector, not by reading it.

stop_if: A fifth vocabulary word is added. RECONCILIATION_VOCABULARY stays at four and #353 says so explicitly; UNKNOWN already means the history needed to judge is unavailable, which is what an unfetched clone has. A reader who needs 'behind' told apart from the other unavailabilities reads the reason, and that wording is asserted.

The reconciliation is given the power to fail the run. It never appends to errors and never changes the exit code. CI checks out with actions/checkout@v7 and no fetch-depth, so every CI run is shallow; a check that could fail there would break every build for a reason that has nothing to do with the repository, which is what #311 keeps out.

The error branch of the reverse `merge-base` call is made to fall through to DIVERGED. At that point exactly one fact is established and it is true of both cases; the call that separates them is the one that failed. A verdict asserted on evidence that was not gathered is the defect #353 is about, restated.

A DIVERGED fixture is asserted in one direction only. Not-an-ancestor alone is also true of a main ref that is merely behind, so a one-way assertion lets a fixture reproducing the opposite condition satisfy a test named for divergence. Both directions, in the fixtures and in the printed reason and in the docstring entry alike.

The printed reason names a CAUSE - a rebase, a force-push, an unrelated line of work. Nothing any call made here can distinguish them, and a reason is one terse assertion in which naming a cause is asserting it. The docstring entry may name causes in order to say they cannot be told apart; that asymmetry is limit 7 of the test module and a WP-112 control measures it.

The live-tree test is made to pin a verdict, a package id or a baseline. WP-112 hardcoded BIZTRUST-GUIDE-WP-111 and merging that package would have broken that package's own test. The id and the baseline are read from badf/current-state.json and the corroboration is over the range; a test whose expectation depends on the record it happens to run against is not a test, and neither is such a control.

`fetch-depth: 0` is added to .github/workflows/pages.yml to make the reconciliation judgeable in CI. That is a separate change with its own review, and it would remove the shallow degradation that four tests and two WP-112 controls are written against.

control/index.html is added to CITING_PAGES in tests/test_html_adr_citations.py, or that module is edited to accommodate a generated page. A regenerated page in the working tree turns the suite red by design; `git checkout -- control/index.html` is the whole fix, and WP-113's checkpoint records the nine failures it produces.

A sentence in any of these files is edited without a command that measures it. Every finding across the last fourteen review rounds on this repository was a sentence that did not match a measurement, and #357 is one of those sentences reaching a fourth file by being copied. Name the command before writing the sentence.

declared_non_coverage: THE ERROR BRANCH OF THE REVERSE `merge-base` CALL IS NEVER REACHED BY THE SUITE. `git merge-base --is-ancestor` answers 0, 1 or an error, and only the first two are constructible without mocking - the identical call in the opposite direction has already succeeded by the time this one runs, so only a timeout or an unrunnable git gets there. Limit 10 of tests/test_resume_reconciliation.py declares it and a control demonstrates it: the branch is mutated to fall through to DIVERGED and the suite is expected to stay GREEN. If that control ever goes red the hole has closed and the limit must be re-derived, not deleted.

NOTHING DISTINGUISHES A STALE REF FROM A DELIBERATELY RESET ONE. A published main line rewound on purpose is an ancestor of the recorded baseline exactly as an unfetched ref is, and both are reported as staleness with the same words. The reflog and the remote would separate them and neither is available to a read-only local call. The reason therefore names the common cause and not the only one.

THREE OF THE FOURTEEN CONTROLS ARE ISOLATED. The runner prints what else each trips. Two suite controls that restore the defect trip the live-tree test as well as the fixture test they are named for, because after this record roll every control clone holds a record ahead of its own origin/main; that is the defect being live in the harness rather than a weakness in the controls, and it is why the two were also run before the roll, where they were isolated. The widest is 'a genuine divergence reported as a stale ref', which trips five tests by design - every test about DIVERGED reads a verdict it makes unreachable.

THE VERDICT IS NOT CHECKED AGAINST THE REST OF THE RECORD. The reconciliation reads two fields - the package id and the baseline - and says nothing about whether `state`, `resume_decision` or `stop_reason` agree with what it found. That is limit 5 of the test module and a WP-112 control measures it green. It is unchanged here.

scripts/wp114_controls.py IS NOT WIRED INTO CI, deliberately, as wp111, wp112 and wp113's runners are not. Every control makes a fresh clone and runs a suite or the validator inside it, which is minutes of work repeated on every push, and validate_continuity.py is the instrument every other gate is read through - a CI step that flaked here would be removed rather than fixed. Its results are evidence about the tree at the commit someone last ran it against, not a standing guarantee, and nothing detects it rotting.

THE #357 CORRECTION IS PROSE PLUS ONE MEASUREMENT CONTROL, NOT A GUARD. Nothing in tests/ fails if a fifth module starts calling a subprocess; the control in scripts/wp114_controls.py would notice, and it is not wired into CI. #357 suggests a ratchet in the shape of tests/test_stale_records.py's registry and that is the right instrument; building it was outside this package's declared scope.

NOTHING HERE VERIFIES GIT'S OWN ANSWER. Both directions of the ancestry question are taken from `git merge-base --is-ancestor` and believed. A git that answered the reverse question wrongly would produce a confident wrong verdict and no test in this repository would notice; the fixtures measure the reconciliation against git, not git against itself.
